text: What will be the nature of flow of water from a circular tap, when its flow rate increased from 0.18 L/min to 0.48 L/min? The radius of the tap and viscosity of water are 0.5 cm and $10^{-3} Pa s$, respectively. (Density of water : $10^{3} kg/m^{3})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Reynolds number for flow rate $Q$ through a tap of diameter $D$, with $v=\dfrac{4Q}{πD^{2}}$:

$R_{e}=\dfrac{ρvD}{η}=\dfrac{4ρQ}{πηD}$

With $D=1\times 10^{-2}\text{m}$ and $Q_{1}=0.18\text{L \min }^{-1}=3\times 10^{-6}\text{m}^{3}\text{s}^{-1}$:

$R_{e1}=\dfrac{4\times 10^{3}\times 3\times 10^{-6}}{π\times 10^{-3}\times 10^{-2}}\approx 382$

With $Q_{2}=0.48\text{L \min }^{-1}=8\times 10^{-6}\text{m}^{3}\text{s}^{-1}$:

$R_{e2}=382\times \dfrac{0.48}{0.18}\approx 1019$

Flow is steady (streamline) for $R_{e}<1000$, unsteady for $1000<R_{e}<2000$ and turbulent for $R_{e}>2000$, so the flow changes from steady to unsteady.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text: The refractive index of a converging lens is 1.4. What will be the focal length of this lens if it is placed in a medium of same refractive index? Assume the radii of curvature of the faces of lens are $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, initially refractive index $(n_{1}) = 1.4$

Then it placed in medium of same refractive index.

$\therefore$ $n_{2} = 1.4$

We know, Focal length

$\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{n_{1}}{n_{2}}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{f}=\left (\frac{1.4}{1.4}-1\right )\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{f}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ f = infinite
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text:
Statement I : A cyclist is moving on an unbanked road with a speed of 7 kmh$^{-1}$ and takes a sharp circular turn along a path of radius of 2m without reducing the speed. The static friction coefficient is 0.2. The cyclist will not slip and pass the curve. $(g = 9.8 m/s^{2})$

Statement II : If the road is banked at an angle of 45${}^{\circ }$, cyclist can cross the curve of 2m radius with the speed of 18.5 kmh$^{-1}$ without slipping.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are true
Statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: on the unbanked road the maximum speed without slipping is

$v_{\max }=\sqrt{μrg}=\sqrt{0.2\times 2\times 9.8}=1.98\text{m s}^{-1}=7.13\text{km h}^{-1}$

Since $7\text{km h}^{-1}<7.13\text{km h}^{-1}$, the cyclist does not slip, so Statement I is correct.

Statement II: on the road banked at $θ=45^{\circ }$ with $μ=0.2$, the speeds without slipping lie between

$v_{\max }=\sqrt{rg\quad \dfrac{\tan θ+μ}{1-μ\tan θ}}=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times \dfrac{1.2}{0.8}}=5.42\text{m s}^{-1}=19.5\text{km h}^{-1}$

$v_{\min }=\sqrt{rg\quad \dfrac{\tan θ-μ}{1+μ\tan θ}}=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times \dfrac{0.8}{1.2}}=3.61\text{m s}^{-1}=13.0\text{km h}^{-1}$

Since $13.0\text{km h}^{-1}<18.5\text{km h}^{-1}<19.5\text{km h}^{-1}$, the cyclist crosses the curve without slipping, so Statement II is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text: A charge Q is moving $\vec{dl}$ distance in the magnetic field $\vec{B}$. Find the value of work done by $\vec{B}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\vec{F}=q\left (\vec{v}\times \vec{B}\right )$

$\therefore$ $\vec{F}⊥\vec{v}$ and $\vec{F}⊥\vec{B}$

Power (p) $=\frac{dw}{dt}$

$=\frac{\vec{F}.\vec{dl}}{dt}$

$=\vec{F}.\frac{\vec{dl}}{dt}$

$=\vec{F}.\vec{v}$

$=Fv\cos θ$

$=Fv\cos 90^{\circ }$

$=0$

As power supply by the field is zero so, total work done also zero.

text: In order to determine the Young's Modulus of a wire of radius 0.2 cm (measured using a scale of least count = 0.001 cm) and length 1m (measured using a scale of least count = 1 mm), a weight of mass 1 kg (measured using a scale of least count = 1 g) was hanged to get the elongation of 0.5 cm (measured using a scale of least count 0.001 cm). What will be the fractional error in the value of Young's Modulus determined by this experiment?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{\Delta Y}{Y}=\left (\frac{\Delta m}{m}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta g}{g}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta A}{A}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta l}{l}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta L}{L}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{1g}{1kg}\right )+0+2\left (\frac{\Delta r}{r}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta l}{l}\right )+\left (\frac{\Delta L}{L}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{1g}{1kg}\right )+2\left (\frac{0.001cm}{0.2cm}\right )+\left (\frac{0.001cm}{0.5cm}\right )+\left (\frac{0.001m}{1m}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{1}{1000}\right )+2\left (\frac{1\times 10}{2\times 10^{3}}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{5}\times \frac{10^{2}}{10^{3}}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{10^{3}}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{1000}+\frac{1}{100}+\frac{2}{10^{3}}+\frac{1}{10^{3}}$

$=\frac{1+10+2+1}{1000}=\frac{14}{1000}\times 100%$

$=1.4%$

text:
The magnetic field in a region is given by $\vec{B}=B_{o}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\widehat{k}$. A square loop of side d is placed with its edges along the x and y axes. The loop is moved with a constant velocity $\vec{v}$ $= v_{0}\hat{i}$. The emf induced in the loop is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Consider the square loop at any instant $t$, when its left edge (parallel to the $Y$-axis) is at the coordinate $x$ and its right edge (also parallel to the $Y$-axis) is at the coordinate $x+d$.


[IMG]


When a straight conducting segment $⃗{l}$ moves with velocity $⃗{v}$ in a magnetic field $⃗{B}$, every free charge carrier $q$ in it experiences the magnetic Lorentz force $⃗{F}_{m}=q(⃗{v}\times ⃗{B})$.

The emf induced across a small element $d⃗{l}$ of the segment is the work done per unit positive charge by this force along $d⃗{l}$, and the emf of the whole segment is the sum of these over its length.

$de=(⃗{v}\times ⃗{B})\cdot d⃗{l}$

$de=\left [\left (v_{0}\hat{i}\right )\times B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\hat{k}\right ]\cdot d⃗{l}=\left [v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )(\hat{i}\times \hat{k})\right ]\cdot d⃗{l}$

$de=\left [-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\hat{j}\right ]\cdot d⃗{l}$

For the horizontal sides $AB$ and $DC$, every small length element $d⃗{l}=dx\hat{i}$ points along the $X$-axis.


[IMG]


$de_{\text{horizontal}}=\left [-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\hat{j}\right ]\cdot \left (dx\hat{i}\right )=0$

So, no emf is induced along either horizontal side of the square loop.

For the vertical side $DA$ at position $x$, the magnetic field is the same along its whole length $d$.


[IMG]


Taking $d⃗{l}=dy\hat{j}$ from the bottom $(y=0)$ to the top $(y=d)$,

$e_{DA}=\int\limits _{0}^{d}\left [-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\hat{j}\right ]\cdot \left (dy\hat{j}\right )=-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )d$

The negative sign shows that the magnetic force pushes positive charges downward (along $-\hat{j}$), so the corner $D$ is at a higher potential than the corner $A$ by $e_{1}=v_{0}B_{0}\left (\dfrac{x}{a}\right )d$.

For the vertical side $CB$ at position $x+d$, the magnetic field is again the same along its whole length $d$. Taking $d⃗{l}=dy\hat{j}$ from the bottom $(y=0)$ to the top $(y=d)$,

$e_{CB}=\int\limits _{0}^{d}\left [-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x+d}{a}\right )\hat{j}\right ]\cdot \left (dy\hat{j}\right )=-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x+d}{a}\right )d$

Again the magnetic force pushes positive charges downward (along $-\hat{j}$), so the corner $C$ is at a higher potential than the corner $B$ by $e_{2}=v_{0}B_{0}\left (\dfrac{x+d}{a}\right )d$.


[IMG]


Both these cells have their positive ends at the bottom ($D$ and $C$), so round the closed loop they oppose each other.

In the closed square loop, the net emf induced is therefore $e_{\text{net}}=e_{2}-e_{1}$.

$e_{\text{net}}=v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x+d}{a}\right )d-v_{0}B_{0}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )d$

$e_{\text{net}}=\frac{v_{0}B_{0}d}{a}[(x+d)-x]=\frac{B_{0}v_{0}d^{2}}{a}$

The result does not depend on $x$. In particular, when the edges of the loop lie along the axes $(x=0)$, the field on side $DA$ is zero, so $e_{1}=0$ and the whole emf comes from side $CB$.

Therefore, the emf induced in the loop is $\dfrac{B_{0}v_{0}d^{2}}{a}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift

text:
A solid disc of radius 'a' and mass 'm' rolls down without slipping on an inclined plane making an angle $θ$ with the horizontal. The acceleration of the disc will be $\frac{2}{b}$g sin$θ$ where b is $____________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer) (g = acceleration due to gravity, $θ$ = angle as shown in figure)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that, on an inclined plane

Acceleration, $a=\frac{g\sin θ}{1+\frac{I}{mR2}}$

$\Rightarrow a=\frac{g\sin θ}{1+\frac{1}{2}}$ [$\because$ For disc, $I=\frac{mR^{2}}{2}$]

$\Rightarrow a=\frac{2}{3}g\sin θ$ ....... (i)

As per question, acceleration of the disc will be $\frac{2}{b}g\sin θ$.

Comparing it with Eq. (i), we get

$b=3$

text: The energy dissipated by a resistor is 10 mJ in 1 s when an electric current of 2 mA flows through it. The resistance is $___________\Omega$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer)

Time, t = 1 s

Resistance, R = ?

$\Rightarrow R=\frac{10^{-2}}{4\times 10^{-6}}\Rightarrow R=0.25\times 10^{4}$

$\Rightarrow R=2500\Omega$

text: A body of mass 2 kg moves under a force of $\left (2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\widehat{k}\right )$N. It starts from rest and was at the origin initially. After 4s, its new coordinates are (8, b, 20). The value of b is $_____________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{F}=(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\widehat{k})N$

time = 4 sec

As body start from rest therefore 
position vector initially $\vec{r_{i}}=(0\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+0\widehat{k})$ & 
u (initial velocity) = 0

given, $r_{f}=(x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k})$

Now, from second equation of motion

$\vec{s}=\vec{u}t+\frac{1}{2}\vec{a}t^{2}$

$r_{f}-r_{i}=\frac{1}{2}\times \left (\frac{2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\widehat{k}}{2}\right )\times (4)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k})-(0\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+0\widehat{k})=8\hat{i}+12\hat{j}+20\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}=8\hat{i}+12\hat{j}+20\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ The value of b = 12

text: A closed organ pipe of length L and an open organ pipe contain gases of densities $ρ_{1}$ and $ρ_{2}$ respectively. The compressibility of gases are equal in both the pipes. solution.body:
First overtone of open pipe $=\frac{v_{2}}{L_{2}}$

First overtone of closed pipe at one end $=\frac{3v}{4L}$

As per question,

$\frac{3V}{4L}=\frac{V_{2}}{L}$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{B}{ρ_{1}}}.\frac{3}{4L}=\sqrt{\frac{B}{ρ_{2}}}.\frac{1}{L_{2}}$ ($\because$ $V=\sqrt{\frac{B}{ρ}}$)

$\Rightarrow L_{2}=\frac{4L}{3}\sqrt{\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}}$ ..... (i)

According to question, the length of the open pipe is

$\frac{x}{3}L\sqrt{\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}}$ ..... (ii)

Comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$x=4$

where, $V_{MR} =$ velocity of man = 12 km/h

and $v_{R} =$ velocity of water flow in river = 6 km/h

As, $v_{MR}$ should be along CD.

$\Rightarrow v_{R}-v_{MR}\sin θ=0$

$\Rightarrow 6-12\sin θ=0\Rightarrow \sin θ=\frac{6}{12}$

$\Rightarrow \sin θ=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow θ=\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\sin ^{-1}(\sin 30^{\circ })$ [$\because$ $\sin 30^{\circ }=\frac{1}{2}$]

$\Rightarrow θ=30^{\circ }$

$\therefore$ $α=90^{\circ }+θ=90^{\circ }+30^{\circ }=120^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow α=120^{\circ }$

text: A force $\vec{F}$ = $4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$ is applied on an intersection point of x = 2 plane and x-axis. The magnitude of torque of this force about a point (2, 3, 4) is $___________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{τ}=\vec{r}\times \vec{F}$

$=\left [(2-2)\hat{i}+(0-3)\hat{j}+(0-4)\widehat{k}\right ]\times (4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k})$

$=(-3\hat{j}-4\widehat{k})\times (4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k})$

$=-16\hat{j}+12\widehat{k}$

$|\vec{τ}|=20$ units
